findings.title: Global group canManage() grants manage rights for VIEW permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the Groups resource type. This method is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup through requireManage(), so a permission that only grants view on all groups allows creating or moving top-level groups. Global manage should require MANAGE only.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. Callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser and UsersResource.getUsersCount expect group IDs, but authorization resource IDs are internal IDs. The loop also processes the type resource named Groups. As a result, user search and count can filter on wrong IDs and return incorrect or empty results when group member-view permissions are used. The code should skip the type resource and add the resource name, which is the group ID.

findings.title: Individual authorization resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates individual resources for users, clients, and groups with a name and scopes but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to enumerate group resources, so individually created group resources will not be found. This breaks enumeration of group-scoped permissions for user search and counts.

findings.title: V2 group permissions throw UnsupportedOperationException from existing lifecycle/API paths
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but existing code still calls it. AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on GroupRemovedEvent, and GroupResource.setManagementPermissionsEnabled calls it through the groups management/permissions endpoint. When V2 is active this can cause group deletion events to fail or the REST endpoint to return 500, and no cleanup of group authorization resources is performed.

findings.title: Group permission evaluation does not filter granted permissions by resource ID
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission evaluates permissions for a group resource but does not filter returned Permission objects by resource ID. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission performs this filter, which is necessary when evaluation can include permissions attached to the resource type or other resources. Without the filter, all-groups permissions may be treated as granted during group-specific checks even when a specific group resource exists, potentially bypassing intended restrictions or negative permissions.

findings.title: getScope can throw NullPointerException for unknown resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking whether resourceType is null or whether the map lookup returns null. A null or unknown resource type will cause a NullPointerException instead of a validation error, turning invalid input into a 500 response.

findings.title: getOrCreateResource throws IllegalStateException for unknown entity IDs
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource throws IllegalStateException when resolveGroup, resolveUser, or resolveClient returns null. A REST caller creating a scope permission with a non-existent group, user, or client ID can trigger a 500 response instead of a 400/404 validation error.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve group resource names
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName only resolves user resources. For group resources it returns resource.getDisplayName(), but individual group resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. Admin UI or policy representations will therefore show an empty value or internal ID instead of the group name.
